Why do we dream? What science knows so far.
No settled answer: one review links dreams to mind wandering, threat rehearsal has mixed support, and a back-of-brain hot zone tracks dreaming in REM and non-REM sleep.

items.caption:
An epidemic left people frozen for decades.
Encephalitis lethargica, the "sleeping sickness" of the 1910s and 1920s, left some survivors motionless for decades. In 1969 Oliver Sacks treated them with L-dopa, the story of his book Awakenings.
